correctness.rationale: Strong Markov and spatial translation yield iid adjacent-site passages, and reflection gives independence of passage time and sign. On the central half-cell, with K=r+z and b=sqrt(K/D), the solution is f(z)(r+z cosh(bx))/K. On the exterior half-cell it is [r+z cosh(b(ℓ-x))]/K plus a multiple of sinh(b(ℓ-x)); matching eliminates that multiple and gives f=(z+r cosh a)/(r cosh a+z cosh 2a). Thus 1/f=1+z A(z) with A(z)=2sinh²(a_z)/(z+r cosh a_z), so μ=A(0) and CV²=1-2A′(0)/μ², yielding the claimed expression. For the pole step, the survival numerator in time is E[exp(kX_t);τ>t]. It is bounded by exp(|k|ℓ) times an exponentially small survival probability (a fixed reset-free interval has a uniform positive probability of Brownian exit). Its transform is analytic in a strip. The explicit f decays as exp(-c sqrt(|Im z|)) high in a narrower strip by the hyperbolic-cosine formula. At k=0, nonlattice τ excludes all other imaginary-axis roots, and f′(0)=-μ supplies simplicity. Compactness on bounded frequencies and the high-frequency bound give an isolated dominant pole for all sufficiently small complex k. After subtracting the survival term, the transformed renewal expression has the decaying factor cosh(kℓ)f(z), so contour shifting gives a locally uniform exponential remainder and justifies differentiating the logarithmic expansion. Expanding cosh(kℓ)f(Λ)=1 gives fourth rate ℓ⁴(3m₂-5μ²)/μ³. The series for 2F has vanishing linear and cubic terms and positive higher coefficients by (9/4)^n>2n+1 for n≥3 and direct n=2. The upper bound follows from the strictly positive higher coefficients of α(cosh(2α)+3)-4sinh α. The endpoint expansions give both sharp bounds and the stated small- and large-rate fourth-coefficient limits. Independent numerical evaluation with ℓ=D=1 at α=1.606115298802767 gives CV²≈0.7216066686, D_eff≈1.1692300894, fourth rate≈0.3854250203 and excess prefactor≈0.07048228031. The supplied checker was read, not run.
